newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philipine rebels declare Christmas ceasefire. [CORRECTED 12:46 GMT 24/12]
newsitem.headline: Philipine rebels declare Christmas ceasefire. [CORRECTED 12:46 GMT 24/12]

text.p: Philippine Communist rebels on Tuesday declared a 10-day Christmas and New Year holiday ceasefire and accused the government of violating its own unilateral truce.

The guerrilla ceasefire took effect from Tuesday and would last until January 2 (corrects from February 2), said a statement from the Communist Party of Philippines sent to news organisations in Manila.
The government declared its own unilateral ceasefire from December 1 to January 29, the longest suspension of military operations against the rebels announced by Manila.

The rebel statement denounced the government ceasefire as a sham, however, saying at least one guerrilla and two leftist sympathisers had been killed in continuing military operations in rural areas this month.
"There will be no genuine peace until the plagues of this country are stamped out," it said.
Manila has started talks with the rebels to try to end a 27-year-old Marxist insurgency, but negotiations broke down after the military refused to release a rebel officer it captured last month.
The government signed a peace pact with the main Moslem rebel group in the southern Philippines in October ending a 24-year revolt.
